SQL:
SELECT
  customers.region_id AS "orders.customers.region_id",
  CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.revenue",
  COUNT(*) AS "orders.n"
FROM orders AS orders
LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
  ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
WHERE
  orders.order_date >= CAST('2025-01-01' AS DATE)
  AND orders.order_date < CAST('2025-04-01' AS DATE)
GROUP BY
  customers.region_id
LIMIT 21

args.message: Q1 2025 (Jan 1 – Mar 31) revenue by region, summing order amounts across all 449 orders: South 10,009.61; North 8,433.41; East 6,593.26; West 3,770.98. Total is 28,807.26. Customers were matched to regions with a left join, so orders without a known region were kept. In this quarter, though, every order has a customer with a known region, so the "no known region" group is empty and doesn't appear in the table. The Arctic region had no orders in Q1. Orders of every status, including "bad", are counted.
